deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics. It is a German-language personal or autobiographical note, written on a sheet that ended up among the notes on pseudo-line arrangements. The previous and next pages classify 1-dimensional arrangements of N pseudo-lines (types I_N, I_{p,q}, II_N, III_6, IV_7). The page begins mid-sentence ('...liest Deutsch'), so it continues a discussion of which language to use. Grothendieck considers writing everything directly 'autobiographical' in French. He then asks whether in-depth meditations based on German-language material should also be written in French. Next he considers running the 'two above approaches' at the same time. One is a chronological investigation of his life, begun immediately. The other is reading material such as his correspondence with 'Hank.' (most plausibly Hanka, the name his mother Johanna went by). The right column continues after a gap. He fears that a strictly chronological approach would leave him constantly trying to 'glue together non-existent memories' ('nichtvorhandenen Erinnerungen zusammenzukitten'). Starting instead from the source material, 'core questions' would emerge and be examined, and other periods might then demand investigation. Once the 'core period' or the source material had been worked through for now, the time might be 'riper' to follow a chronological order. The page breaks off at 'Jedenfalls...'. In short, it is a methodological plan for an autobiographical or introspective meditation. It is undated here; the file is catalogued as 'from 1981 on', which would put it around or just before Récoltes et Semailles (1983-86) and the later work on his parents (La Clef des Songes, 1987).

ideas.what: Plan for an autobiographical meditation: choice of language (German vs French) and method (chronological reconstruction vs starting from documents such as correspondence, letting 'core questions' emerge before attempting chronology)
ideas.where_published: Related themes appear in Récoltes et Semailles and La Clef des Songes (the section on his parents). This specific German draft plan is not known to me in published form.

missed.claim: A German-language working note in which Grothendieck plans an autobiographical investigation. It weighs French against German and proposes reading his correspondence with (probably) Hanka, his mother, in parallel with a chronological life review. It sits physically inside the pseudo-line arrangement notes (from 1981 on).
missed.quote: eine chronologische Untersuchung über mein Leben sofort anzufangen, und zur gleichen Zeit die Lektüre etwa meines Briefwechsels mit Hank[a?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of biographical rather than mathematical interest. It documents the interleaving of combinatorial-geometry work with the start of introspective writing. It also shows German being considered as a working language for the meditations, and may help date the genesis of his writing about his parents.

deep.surprise_reason: No mathematics. It is a minor biographical document of mild interest to historians, mainly for dating the onset of his autobiographical projects and the use of German.
transcription_corrections: Last line of left column: 'mit Hans[?]' is more likely 'mit Hank[a]' (abbreviated 'Hank.'), probably his mother Hanka.

Right column: 'möglicherweise aus andern Perioden [-sich...-] zur Untersuchung aufdrängen' should read roughly 'möglicherweise auch andere Perioden sich zur Untersuchung aufdrängen' (with a struck-through attempt).
'nichtvorhandenen Erinnerungen zusammenkitten' should be 'zusammenzukitten zu versuchen' (the line break splits 'zusammen-/kitten').

'würden [-sich-] sicher sich Kernfragen [-...-] {+auffinden+}': the struck word under 'auffinden' is illegible. The sense is that core questions would be found and examined ('untersucht' replaces struck 'behandelt').
'Kernperio-de' at the line end means 'Kernperiode' (core period).
